chats.answer:
The power station that takes the fewest hours of sunlight to fully recharge with two solar panels depends on three things:

Battery capacity (Wh): Smaller batteries recharge faster.

Solar input limit (W): Higher input allows faster charging.

Panel wattage: Two 400W panels recharge much faster than two 100W panels.

The key is the ratio of battery capacity to usable solar charging power.

chats.answer:
The power station that recharges fastest with two solar panels depends on three things:

Battery capacity (Wh): Smaller batteries take fewer hours to refill.

Maximum solar input (W): Higher input allows faster charging.

Panel wattage: Two 400W panels can charge much faster than two 100W panels.

For example, a 1,000Wh power station accepting 800W of solar input could theoretically recharge in 1.25 hours at full output, but realistically it may take around 1.5–2.5 hours of strong sunlight.

The key metric is battery capacity ÷ usable solar charging power, not simply which station has the biggest battery or fastest AC charging.
